entries: Miradouro da Rocha do Navio
Look across the marine reserve towards Ilhéu da Viúva from Santana's cliffs.
The place name recalls a Dutch shipwreck in the nineteenth century.
Miradouro da Santinha
A roadside panorama of Porto Moniz, its volcanic pools and Ilhéu Mole.
A figure of Nossa Senhora dos Caminhos reflects local religious traditions.
Miradouro do Parque de Merendas dos Lamaceiros
A picnic-park viewpoint above Ribeira da Janela, beside the start of its levada.
The surrounding irrigation channel connects this leisure area with Madeira's agricultural landscape.
Miradouro do Pico — Porto Moniz
A clifftop lookout above Porto Moniz at the end of Caminho do Pico.
This former royal road carried people and goods between local villages.
Miradouro do Teleférico das Achadas da Cruz
See the coastal fields of Fajã da Quebrada Nova below the cable-car station.
The cable connection was developed to help farmers reach and transport their crops.
Miradouro do Porto de Abrigo
A low waterfront perspective from Porto Moniz's pier towards the Ribeira da Janela islets.
The historic pier and eighteenth-century fountain recall the town's fishing heritage.
Miradouro do Ribeiro Frio
A forest panorama beside ER103 in São Roque do Faial, near popular walking routes.
The landscape preserves native Laurissilva woodland; the source gives no viewpoint founding date.
Miradouro das Cruzinhas
Look into the upper Ribeira Seca valley from ER103 above Faial.
Cultivated terraces beside the forest reveal the area's agricultural landscape.
Miradouro do Lombo dos Palheiros
A lookout beside São Roque do Faial's cemetery, facing mountain villages and Penha d'Águia.
The settlement lies between the Ribeira da Metade and Ribeira do Castelejo valleys.
Miradouro das Empenas
A mountain-road panorama stretching from São Jorge towards Ponta de São Lourenço.
The official account describes a natural lookout, without dating its establishment.
Miradouro do Picarouto
A stop in Pico das Pedras Forest Park overlooking Penha d'Águia and the eastern coast.
Its setting combines native Laurissilva vegetation with introduced tree species.
Miradouro da Cova da Roda
A north-coast lookout reached along an old cobbled approach, with Penha d'Águia ahead.
The approach belonged to an early road linking Funchal with Santana.
Miradouro de Nossa Senhora dos Bons Caminhos
An ER101 lookout over Faial and the Atlantic, marked by a religious statue.
Its dedication expresses the local tradition of faith along travel routes.
Miradouro do Curtado
From Santana's road, look towards Faial's rugged coast and Penha d'Águia.
Also written Cortado, this lookout has no founding date in the consulted source.
Miradouro de Santo António — Santana
Views take in Achada do Gramacho, vineyards and part of Rocha do Navio.
The marine reserve visible below was established in 1997.
Miradouro da Quinta do Furão
A hotel-estate lookout above Santana's northeast cliffs, overlooking Ilhéu da Viúva.
Traditional vineyards remain part of the estate's cultivated landscape.
Miradouro do Cabeço do Resto
A high viewpoint in Ilha overlooking Santana, São Jorge and the surrounding settlements.
Its name refers to a headland enclosed by streams.
Miradouro das Eiras
Near Pico da Rainha, look into Ilha's densely wooded stream valleys.
Ilha's name describes land enclosed by streams: an island within the island.
Miradouro do Pico — São Jorge
Look across the mouth of Ribeira de São Jorge towards the surrounding mountains.
The official account describes the natural setting, without dating the viewpoint's establishment.
Miradouro da Vigia — São Jorge
A coastal lookout with views westwards from Arco de São Jorge towards Porto Moniz.
This strategically placed lookout was formerly used to spot whales.
Miradouro do Ninho da Manta
A walking viewpoint on PR1 near Pico do Areeiro, overlooking Fajã da Nogueira.
Its name is traditionally linked to buzzards believed to have nested here.
Miradouro da Beira da Quinta
Look over Arco de São Jorge and the northwest coast from a 469-metre-high vantage point.
The source records the landscape, but gives no founding date.
Miradouro da Boca das Voltas
A secluded Boaventura lookout towards Falcas, Achada da Madeira and Lombo do Urzal.
The forest setting preserves the region's native Laurissilva landscape.
Miradouro do Cabo Aéreo
A São Jorge coastal viewpoint overlooking Calhau and the remains of old mills.
A transport cable once moved produce, including sugar cane, down the cliffs.
Miradouro da Boca dos Namorados
A Jardim da Serra lookout towards Curral das Freiras and Eira do Serrado.
Jardim da Serra became a separate parish in March 1996.
Miradouro da Boca da Corrida
A high mountain viewpoint over Curral das Freiras, beside the PR12 trailhead.
The historic Caminho Real da Encumeada begins here.
Miradouro do Castelo do Pico
See Funchal Bay from the elevated São João Baptista fortress.
The seventeenth-century fort later housed naval radio communications, inspiring the name Pico Rádio.
Miradouro da Achada — Funchal
A garden lookout on Estrada Dr. João Abel de Freitas, facing eastern Funchal.
Funchal's municipal council created this viewpoint in 2009.
Miradouro da Nazaré
A São Martinho viewpoint above western Funchal, linking city, coast and mountains in one panorama.
The parish was formerly part of São Pedro until the late sixteenth century.
Miradouro da Quinta Vigia
A historic garden estate on Avenida do Infante, looking across Funchal Bay towards Garajau.
Acquired by the regional government in 1979, it became the president's official residence in 1984.
Miradouro da Vila Guida
A garden terrace on Rua Conde Carvalhal framing Funchal Bay.
The viewpoint dates to 1938; an Adriana Lajinha tile panel depicts old Funchal.
Miradouro das Neves
An eastern Funchal lookout over the bay, with the Desertas visible in clear conditions.
The official source describes its elevated setting but does not date its establishment.
Miradouro de São Roque
A church-front viewpoint above Funchal, with benches facing the bay and Atlantic.
The parish dates to 1579; today's church replaced an earlier chapel.
Miradouro do Curral dos Romeiros
A wooded lookout on Caminho dos Pretos, above Funchal and the João Gomes valley.
Nearby reservoirs were built to store water for irrigation.
Miradouro do Forte de São José
A harbour-edge viewpoint on a rocky islet beside Funchal's port.
The eighteenth-century fortress was built to protect the harbour entrance.
Miradouro do Jardim Botânico
Garden terraces above the João Gomes valley offer a broad view of Funchal.
The garden opened in 1960 on the Reid family's former Quinta do Bom Sucesso.
Miradouro do Lido
A low coastal viewpoint in Funchal's hotel district, facing the Atlantic and Lido Islet.
The source describes its seafront setting without recording a founding date.
Miradouro do Lombo da Quinta
A high Boa Nova roadside lookout over Funchal Bay, near Palheiro.
Nearby Palheiro Golf was designed by Cabell B. Robinson in 1993.
Miradouro do Palheiro Ferreiro
A garden-estate viewpoint on the hillside east of Funchal, overlooking the city.
The first Count of Carvalhal established the estate in the early nineteenth century.
Miradouro do Parque de Santa Catarina
A central park viewpoint over Funchal's harbour, with views extending towards Garajau.
Santa Catarina Park opened in 1966 and includes a historic chapel.
Miradouro do Pico dos Barcelos
At 355 metres, this Santo António lookout takes in Funchal's amphitheatre and bay.
Renovations expanded leisure areas and improved access; the source gives no founding date.
Miradouro do Pináculo
A São Gonçalo lookout on Rua Conde Carvalhal, framing Funchal's coast from the east.
The source records its 283-metre elevation, without dating the viewpoint's establishment.
Miradouro do Socorro
A viewpoint in Funchal's old town, above Barreirinha and facing the port.
Santa Maria's historic quarter developed during the first half of the fifteenth century.
Miradouro do Terreiro da Luta
A Monte hillside panorama beside the Nossa Senhora da Paz sanctuary.
The sanctuary commemorates a vow made during the 1917 submarine bombardments of Funchal.
Miradouro dos Marmeleiros
A shaded lookout near Marmeleiros Hospital, overlooking Funchal from the Monte hillside.
The viewpoint was built in 1939, nine years after the hospital opened.
Miradouro do Largo Padre Pita Ferreira
A viewpoint below São Gonçalo church, looking west across Funchal Bay.
It honours a local priest and defender of Madeira's artistic heritage, who died in 1963.
Miradouro da Quinta das Cruzes
A historic São Pedro lookout over central Funchal, surrounded by mature garden trees.
Opened in 1936, the viewpoint occupies an estate associated with João Gonçalves Zarco.
Miradouro das Babosas
A Monte square lookout over the João Gomes valley, near the cable-car stations.
The square's 1906 chapel was destroyed during the floods of February 2010.
Miradouro de Santa Luzia
A hillside viewpoint on Rua da Levada de Santa Luzia, overlooking Funchal.
Its parish, Imaculado Coração de Maria, was established in 1954 as the city expanded.
Miradouro do Pico Alto
A mountain lookout inside Funchal Ecological Park, facing the city and Chão da Lagoa.
The municipal ecological park was created in 1994 for conservation, education and recreation.
Miradouro do Paredão
Two mountain vantage points reveal Curral das Freiras on one side and Funchal on the other.
The official description records the setting but gives no founding date.
Miradouro da Queimada
An Água de Pena lookout over Machico Bay, the airport and Madeira's eastern peninsula.
The source places it on Regional Road 101, without recording a founding date.
Miradouro da Contenda
A quiet Gaula viewpoint towards Santa Cruz, Ponta de São Lourenço and the Desertas.
Gaula's local craft heritage includes the production of Madeira embroidery.
Miradouro de São Sebastião — Ribeira Brava
A clifftop panorama over Ribeira Brava and the south coast towards Ponta do Sol.
The source describes the town's coastal setting but does not date the viewpoint.
Miradouro do Espigão
A São Paulo lookout across Ribeira Brava's valley towards the Serra d'Água peaks.
The source describes the mountainous landscape, without recording a founding date.
Miradouro da Pousada dos Vinháticos
A Serra d'Água viewpoint surrounded by forested slopes and the Cruz, Cedro and Pico Grande peaks.
The viewpoint takes its name from the inn, open since 1933.
Miradouro da Encumeada
From the mountain pass, look into the Ribeira Brava and São Vicente valleys.
The source documents its 1,007-metre elevation but provides no founding date.
Miradouro sobre a Ponta do Sol
A valley-and-ocean panorama above Ponta do Sol, with benches for a short stop.
The town's name refers to a rocky point reflecting sunlight.
Miradouro do Cascalho
A Lombada lookout on ER222, facing Lugar de Baixo, Tabua and Ribeira Brava.
The source describes these coastal settlements without dating the viewpoint's establishment.
Miradouro da Achada de Santo Antão
Also called Farol Verde, this clifftop viewpoint overlooks Arco da Calheta and Madalena do Mar.
Arco da Calheta was among the island's early settlement and farming areas.
Miradouro do Piarro
A Lombo do Doutor lookout above Calheta's beach, marina and Casa das Mudas.
The source describes this coastal panorama but gives no founding date.
Miradouro do Jardim do Mar
Look over Jardim do Mar, where the village occupies a coastal fajã.
The source presents the village's coastal setting without recording a viewpoint founding date.
Miradouro da Raposeira
A high Fajã da Ovelha lookout over Paul do Mar, Jardim do Mar and Prazeres.
The panorama connects farming uplands with Paul do Mar's longstanding fishing community.
Miradouro do Precipício
A steep-cliff lookout on the descent towards Paul do Mar from Fajã da Ovelha.
The surrounding parish was established in the sixteenth century.
Miradouro do Massapez
A Fajã da Ovelha panorama spanning Paul do Mar, Jardim do Mar and Prazeres.
The coastal villages visible below preserve the region's fishing heritage.
Miradouro da Lombada dos Marinheiros
A west-coast lookout towards Fajã da Ovelha and Ponta do Pargo lighthouse.
This viewpoint was created in 1936.
Miradouro do Fio — Fajã da Ovelha
A clifftop outlook over Paul do Mar, near the Fajã Grande path.
Its name recalls a former cable used to carry supplies up the slope.
Miradouro da Boa Morte
A Ponta do Pargo lookout over western cliffs towards Calhau das Achadas da Cruz.
The source reports restoration of the viewpoint and its 250-metre approach, without a date.
Teleférico da Rocha do Navio
Descend from Santana's cliffs towards the coastal fields of Rocha do Navio.
The cable car was originally built to give local farmers access to their fields.
Teleférico das Fajãs do Cabo Girão — Rancho
Travel from Sítio do Rancho down to the cultivated terraces below Cabo Girão.
The cable car initially served farmers accessing their coastal agricultural land.
Teleférico do Jardim Botânico
A separate cable-car line joins Monte's Largo das Babosas with the Botanical Garden.
The operator records entry into service in 2005.
Teleférico do Garajau
Descend from Ponta do Garajau, near Cristo Rei, to the beach below.
The cable car opened in 2007 beside the protected marine reserve.
Teleférico das Achadas da Cruz
A steep descent from Achadas da Cruz to the coast and agricultural plots.
Transporting farmers and their produce was a principal reason for its construction.
Teleférico do Funchal — Monte
Board on Funchal's waterfront for the cable-car journey uphill to Monte.
Construction began in 1999 and the cable car opened in 2000.
